# Azure Resource Manager network client library for Java

Azure Resource Manager network client library for Java

For documentation on how to use this package, please see [Azure Management Libraries for Java](https://aka.ms/azsdk/java/mgmt).

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- [Java Development Kit (JDK)][jdk] with version 8 or above
- [Azure Subscription][azure_subscription]

### Adding the package to your product

[//]: # ({x-version-update-start;com.azure.resourcemanager:azure-resourcemanager-network;current})
```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>com.azure.resourcemanager</groupId>
    <artifactId>azure-resourcemanager-network</artifactId>
    <version>2.62.0</version>
</dependency>
```
[//]: # ({x-version-update-end})

### Include the recommended packages

Azure Management Libraries require a `TokenCredential` implementation for authentication and an `HttpClient` implementation for HTTP client.

[Azure Identity][azure_identity] package and [Azure Core Netty HTTP][azure_core_http_netty] package provide the default implementation.

### Authentication

Microsoft Entra ID token authentication relies on the [credential class][azure_identity_credentials] from [Azure Identity][azure_identity] package.

Azure subscription ID can be configured via `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
Azure tenant ID can be configured via `AZURE_TENANT_ID` environment variable.

Assuming the use of the `DefaultAzureCredential` credential class, the client can be authenticated using the following code:

```java readme-sample-authenticate
AzureProfile profile = new AzureProfile(AzureEnvironment.AZURE);
TokenCredential credential = new DefaultAzureCredentialBuilder()
    .authorityHost(profile.getEnvironment().getActiveDirectoryEndpoint())
    .build();
NetworkManager manager = NetworkManager
    .authenticate(credential, profile);
```

The sample code assumes global Azure. Please change `AzureEnvironment.AZURE` variable if otherwise.

See [Authentication][authenticate] for more options.

omissions.subtype: Certificate bytes and file to Base64
omissions.explanation: The certificate wrapper reads file bytes or accepts bytes, Base64-encodes them, and writes the encoded data to the inner model.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The unannotated implementation class explicitly converts bytes and reads a file around a generated inner certificate model; the captured file has no @Generated members, so provenance is not independently established.

omissions.explanation: The backend health wrapper builds a name-indexed, read-only map of HTTP configuration health wrappers from an inner collection and resolves its backend from the gateway.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: An unannotated implementation constructs nested public wrappers and a map from inner models rather than exposing the inner collection directly; no per-member generation provenance is supplied.

omissions.explanation: The HTTP configuration health wrapper turns inner server-health items into public wrappers indexed by IP address and exposes a read-only map.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: This unannotated implementation explicitly creates child wrappers and a map from inner models, but the capture has no generation-history proof.

omissions.explanation: The backend HTTP configuration setter adds leading and trailing slashes to a non-null path before updating the inner model.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The unannotated fluent implementation changes caller input before the inner-model setter; no annotation or customization-script provenance is captured.

omissions.subtype: Reuse or create gateway authentication certificate
omissions.explanation: A backend HTTP configuration reuses a certificate with matching Base64 data or creates and attaches one, adds its reference without duplicate IDs, and switches the protocol to HTTPS.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The unannotated implementation coordinates parent certificate lookup, conditional creation and inner-model reference updates; the captured source does not establish its generation history.

omissions.explanation: Host-header setters coordinate the hostname and pick-from-backend fields, clearing the conflicting field when the caller selects either mode.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The unannotated wrapper contains explicit coupled inner-model updates rather than a single generated setter; generator provenance is not independently captured.

omissions.explanation: Providing a positive drain timeout creates the inner connection-draining object when needed and sets both its timeout and enabled flag.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: An unannotated fluent method contains conditional nested-model construction and state changes; the request does not prove that these members were manually authored.

omissions.explanation: The backend wrapper initializes its address list if absent and suppresses case-insensitive duplicate IP addresses when adding a backend address.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The unannotated implementation explicitly checks existing addresses before changing an inner model, while generator provenance is unconfirmed.

omissions.subtype: Resolve network interface from health result
omissions.explanation: The server-health wrapper parses an IP-configuration resource ID, fetches its parent network interface, and returns the named IP configuration when available.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The unannotated method traverses parent wrappers and makes a separate network-interface lookup rather than simply returning an inner field; provenance is unconfirmed.

omissions.subtype: Mutually exclusive public and private frontends
omissions.explanation: Selecting a subnet clears the public IP reference; selecting a public IP clears subnet and private-IP settings.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The unannotated frontend wrapper actively clears incompatible inner-model fields in the two setters; manual authorship is plausible but not proven by generation metadata.

omissions.subtype: Hydrate child wrapper maps from inner models
omissions.explanation: The gateway rebuilds named maps of child wrappers from inner-model collections on refresh, including certificates, frontends, backends, rules and configurations.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The unannotated gateway implementation constructs and indexes many public wrappers around generated inner models; the capture does not include generator output comparison.

omissions.subtype: Prune dangling child references before gateway create

omissions.handwrittenRationale: The unannotated lifecycle hook explicitly reconciles public child wrappers and inner reference lists; whether the implementation was manually maintained needs confirmation.

omissions.explanation: Before serializing request-routing rules, the gateway conditionally assigns priorities to newly added rules when the API supports them.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The unannotated lifecycle method calls a custom rule collection to set priorities, but that collection and generator history are not supplied.

omissions.explanation: Before group create or update, the gateway rejects simultaneous legacy WAF settings and a WAF policy and clears legacy settings when a policy is present.
omissions.handwrittenRationale: The unannotated gateway lifecycle hook performs cross-field validation and throws an explicit error; the capture provides no direct generation comparison.

omissions.explanation: The gateway generates and attaches an IP configuration with a random name if none is designated as default before creation.

limitations: Coverage is partial: 2869 discovered files, 2023 eligible files, eight source captures, 225 explicit skipped entries, and zero recorded extraction errors. ApplicationGatewayImpl is only an excerpt of lines 1-493; its skipped entry records that partial capture, not a wholly absent ninth capture. This assessment does not establish absence of customizations in this library.

All eight captured source entries have kind unknown. They contain concrete facade implementations, but no captured customization-script operation, generated baseline, or neighboring generated/unannotated member contrast establishes handwritten ownership. Specialized behavior and absence of @Generated throughout these files are not by themselves sufficient attribution under the supplied guidelines; the findings array therefore excludes uncertain candidates.

Certificate helpers visibly read files, Base64-encode bytes and delegate to setters. Backend HTTP configuration additionally searches existing certificates by content, creates a randomly named parent certificate when needed, attaches references and selects HTTPS. These are observable convenience behaviors, but the supplied source does not establish that they were handwritten rather than produced as part of this facade implementation.

The backend HTTP configuration normalizes nonnull paths to leading and trailing slashes, resolves probe and certificate references, coordinates host-header selection flags, and configures connection draining. These operations are visible; their customization provenance is unresolved. The certificate removal loop and its null behavior are not inferred to be intentional bug fixes.

Backend helpers wrap addresses, derive NIC and IP-configuration names from resource IDs, suppress duplicate IP addresses case-insensitively and remove matching addresses. Health wrappers construct name/IP-keyed maps and return unmodifiable views. Neither these algorithms nor simple enum/property aliases alone prove a handwritten customization, and unmodifiable views are not described as deep immutable snapshots.

Frontend helpers construct subnet references, clear mutually incompatible public/private frontend fields, coordinate allocation modes and retrieve associated resources. The missing Utils helper and parent-chain implementations cannot be inspected from these captures. No behavior beyond the captured call sites, and no universal exclusivity invariant, is assumed.

The gateway excerpt rebuilds child wrapper maps after refresh, gathers task-created resources before create, copies wrappers into inner collections, clears dangling child references, creates default child resources and rejects mixed legacy WAF configuration and WAF policy in the shown branches. Several invoked helpers and the end of ensureDefaultPublicFrontend are outside the excerpt. Concrete orchestration and service-specific validation do not independently establish handwritten ownership or complete lifecycle semantics.

The three complete generation-context captures are the package POM, README and tsp-location.yaml. The POM configures dependencies, tests, module access and coverage exclusions; the README demonstrates authentication; the location file identifies the specification revision. These do not identify per-method handwritten edits. Package and dependency presence, README examples, generated paging or ordinary asynchronous delegation are not counted as customizations.

All 225 supplied skipped path/reason entries were considered, including the partial gateway capture, implementation collections, resource/model facades, shared helpers and NetworkManager. Uncaptured source, public interfaces, generation tooling and historical baselines were not fetched or inferred. The recorded zero capture errors is not exhaustive discovery assurance; no LRO, paging, authentication or other package-wide absence claim is made.
No analyst proposals were supplied; these 15 findings are candidate omissions only, inconclusive and UNCOUNTED pending an independent assessment of provenance and classification.

Only eight of 2,023 eligible source files were captured from 2,869 discovered files, with 225 entries skipped for review budget and no recorded extraction errors. The captured ApplicationGatewayImpl.java ends at line 493 mid-method; no absence or completeness claim is possible.

Captured implementation files are unannotated and wrap generated inner types, but lack adjacent @Generated markers, customization-script edits, generated-output comparisons or version history. Manual authorship and generator addressability cannot be established conclusively from the supplied material.

The captured POM, README and TypeSpec location identify packaging, authentication usage and specification location, not the provenance of individual wrapper methods. Several referenced interfaces, child implementations and AddedRuleCollection are outside the evidence; behavior attributed to those components is not assumed.
